title: Measure a robot joint's lost motion with controlled opposing pulls
instruction: Characterize the mounted robot servo's lost motion using the two connected spring gauges. Allow both gauges to remain unloaded for two seconds. Grip a gauge body and pull along its loading line until its reading is 1.2–1.8 N, with the opposite gauge at or below 0.10 N. Hold the force and angle steady for two seconds, then unload both gauges for two seconds. Repeat for the opposite direction. Leave both gauges released and unloaded for two seconds. The recorder automatically saves the force and angle samples. Do not push the servo, lever or exposed gauge eyelets, change the servo setting, disturb the fixture, or reach 2.0 N for 0.2 seconds.
context: On a robot-development bench, characterize how a mounted geared actuator responds when the load reverses. Controlled opposite pulls and complete unloads produce force-and-output-angle records for comparing actuators used in robot joints. The robot must maintain the test load without loading the opposite link or directly pushing the output lever. This adapts an open-source servo characterization method; it measures effective lost motion, including compliance, rather than adjusting the joint or targeting a desired backlash value.
setup: A fixed YAM station table, 1.1 x 1.3 m, surface z=0.7475 m, holds a 450 x 300 x 16 mm rigid mounting plate centred at (0.345, 0) m, its long side along world Y. A printed-polymer-look holder with 44 x 70 mm footprint supports a 42 x 40 x 50 mm geared-servo proxy. The horizontal output shaft is at (0.345, 0, 0.8575) m; a 100 mm printed lever points upward to a common loading eye. Two opposed 180 mm relaxed elastic links connect that eye to dynamic spring-gauge bodies centred at (0.345, +/-0.250, 0.9605) m. Each white polymer-look gauge is 140 x 20 x 18 mm, 80 g, with metal-look eyelets and a visible 0-2 N pointer; it rests freely in a 160 x 26 x 8 mm open cradle and is grasped by its body. A fixed black 320 x 170 x 48 mm recorder at (0.100, 0, table height) has two force scales with green 1.2-1.8 N bands and an output-angle scale. Pointers display the force and encoder channels; the recorder saves samples automatically. Both arms start at standard READY, both links unloaded, the servo input held at zero. No layout jitter. LAYOUT.md supplies exact geometry, ordinary-part sourcing, CAD and the proposed calibrated camera/UART acquisition chain; this adaptation has not been built in hardware.
scoring:
A qualifying direction consists of a consecutive two-second loaded window followed by a consecutive two-second unloaded window, after the initial two-second unloaded baseline. Either direction may be first. Samples are recorded at 10 Hz. During loading, active force must remain 1.2–1.8 N, opposite force at most 0.10 N, active force range at most 0.20 N, encoder range at most two counts (4096 counts/revolution), and a conservative alignment error atan2(|transverse X offset| + |vertical offset|, |horizontal Y offset|) at most 10 degrees. During unloading, both forces must be at most 0.10 N and encoder range at most two counts.

- **0:** no complete direction record, or a latched overload/fixture/link/setting violation.
- **0.5:** one complete direction record; also the score for two records without the final release condition.
- **1.0:** both opposite-direction records, stored raw samples and computed loaded/unloaded reversal values, and both gauges released and unloaded for two consecutive seconds at the end.

Repeated measurements of the same direction cannot replace the other direction. Direct contact with the protected servo/lever/exposed gauge eyelets or invalid telemetry clears the measurements and requires a fresh unloaded baseline. Opposite loading before completing unloading invalidates that pending record. Overload of at least 2.0 N for at least 0.2 seconds, fixture displacement, link failure or a changed servo setting latches zero. Final release is evaluated from the current state, not a permanently retained maximum score. No desired backlash value, particular hand assignment or exact home pose is required. Fixture displacement of 5 mm or 3 degrees, a link reaching 230 mm, or departure from the held zero servo setting is an integrity failure. Release requires open grippers and both tool centres more than 40 mm from either gauge body. Contact exclusion uses geometric envelopes around the servo, lever and exposed eyelets, including sampled distal arm links; it is a conservative proxy, not a contact-force sensor. Force limits are acquisition rules, not manufacturer damage limits.
reset_notes: Return gauge bodies to their open cradles, unload both links, restore the upright lever and zero held input, return arms to READY, and clear acquisition windows, records and violation latches. Keep fixture, recorder and camera positions unchanged. Begin with two seconds of unloaded baseline; no expendable parts.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies and limited revolute joints approximate a held geared servo. Tension-only elastic laws apply equal/opposite loads to free gauge bodies and the lever; gauge internals and cords are not resolved. Force pointers are simulated readouts; output angle is quantized to 4096 counts/revolution. Contact exclusion is geometric. Effective lost motion includes compliance; the proposed physical readout chain is uncalibrated. One fixed layout is demonstrated.
scores: Scripted continuous YAM demo: 1.0 in 536 steps (26.8 s). Dream-1 beta through Inspect Robots: 0.0 at the 2,400-step limit (120 s), one completed trial with zero errored trials, same scene and scorer.
